rationale: The child is an unpublished, person-specific order authorizing a competitive appointment. C25 is the closest candidate because it concerns competitive status and civil-service protections, but it addresses separation from excepted positions rather than authorization of an individual's appointment and supplies no demonstrated shared drafting. C23 is another person-specific civil-service exception, but its machinery concerns reemployment rights after international-organization service. C13 contains appointment authority within Selective Service regulations, but only as part of a broad administrative scheme. None plausibly supplied a concrete and material drafting template for the child.
